# `erasure` operations

The exact fields each `erasure.*` operation takes and returns.

<!-- Generated by `python scripts/codegen/docs_reference.py` from the op registry; edit the models, not this page. -->

Every op is `POST /v1/<op>` over HTTP and the MCP tool `loom_<op>`. The identity fields (`org`, `namespace`, `agent`, `user_id`, `session_id`) are filled from the token and the MCP session when a transport can; see [identities and namespaces](../../concepts/identities-and-namespaces.md). The [operations index](../operations.md) explains role, kind and the MCP `all` listing. Unknown input fields are served and named in `ignored_args`.

<!-- prettier-ignore-start -->

## `erasure.export`

GDPR Article 20 portability.

`POST /v1/erasure.export` · MCP `loom_erasure_export` · role `admin` · idempotent · audited

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `scope_type` | `Literal['user_id', 'namespace', 'namespace_list']` | required | `user_id` exports one user's rows across the org (org admin only); `namespace` exports one namespace (admin on it). |
| `scope_value` | `str` | required | The user id or namespace to export. |
| `requester` | `str` | required | email or service account requesting the export |
| `include_tombstoned` | `bool` | `True` | Include tombstoned memory and conversation rows. |
| `section_limit` | `int` | `10000` | Per-section caps. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exported_at` | `datetime` | When the export was read (UTC). |
| `org` | `str` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `scope_type` | `Literal['user_id', 'namespace', 'namespace_list']` | Echo of the requested scope kind. |
| `scope_value` | `str` | Echo of the requested user id or namespace. |
| `requester` | `str` | Echo of who asked for the export. |
| `counts` | `dict[str, int]` | Rows returned per section (`memory`, `knowledge`, `conversations`, `conversation_threads`, `agent_events`, `audit_log`): at most `section_limit`, and the section's `truncated` says more exist. |
| `memory` | `ErasureExportSection` | `loom.memory` rows in scope (under the Postgres authority, its heads); tombstoned rows too when `include_tombstoned`. |
| `knowledge` | `ErasureExportSection` | Knowledge chunk rows of the namespace, or every one the user wrote for a `user_id` scope. |
| `conversations` | `ErasureExportSection` | Turns and saved messages in scope with their `sensitivity`, up to `erasure_export_conversation_max_bytes` of text plus the turn that crosses it. |
| `conversation_threads` | `ErasureExportSection` | Threads in scope with their title, metadata and `sensitivity`, capped by `section_limit` rows only (no byte budget). |
| `agent_events` | `ErasureExportSection` | Per-request ledger rows in scope, newest first. |
| `audit_log` | `ErasureExportSection` | Audit rows in scope; for `user_id`, rows whose subject mentions the user id. |

## `erasure.list`

Audit-shaped roll-up of the org's erasures the caller may see: the org-wide view for an org admin, the namespace sagas of the caller's own namespaces otherwise.

`POST /v1/erasure.list` · MCP `loom_erasure_list` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `limit` | `int` | `50` | At most this many sagas, newest first; the server caps it at 500. |
| `status` | `Literal['in_progress', 'completed', 'failed'] \| None` | `None` | filter to one status if needed |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` | `list[ErasureListRow]` | Recent sagas, newest first: org-wide for an org admin, otherwise only `namespace` sagas on namespaces the caller belongs to. |

## `erasure.request`

GDPR Article 17 forgetting.

`POST /v1/erasure.request` · MCP `loom_erasure_request` · role `writer` · idempotent · audited

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `org` | `str` | required | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `scope_type` | `Literal['user_id', 'namespace', 'namespace_list']` | required | What `scope_value` names: `user_id` (one user across the org's namespaces, org admin only), `namespace` (one namespace, admin on it) or `namespace_list` (several, org admin only). |
| `scope_value` | `str` | required | For `namespace_list`: a JSON array of namespace names (1–500), or a JSON object {"namespaces": [...], "purge": bool}. |
| `requester` | `str` | required | email or service account that requested the erasure |
| `urgency` | `Literal['normal', 'urgent']` | `'normal'` | `normal` or `urgent`; recorded on the saga's ledger row, the saga runs the same either way. |
| `purge` | `bool` | `False` | Hard-delete the rows of the soft-delete tables (memory, embeddings, chunks, documents, summaries, links) instead of stamping tombstoned_at: a tombstone keeps the bytes in every FINAL read and merge; a purge takes them out of the parts. |
| `external` | `bool` | `True` | External backends (Langfuse traces by tag, ClickStack OTel rows, …) run for every namespace of the scope and fail the saga closed. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `erasure_id` | `str` | Id of the saga; pass it to `erasure.status`. |
| `status` | `Literal['in_progress', 'completed', 'failed']` | `completed`, or `failed` when a step or the residue check failed; the recovery worker retries a failed saga. |
| `steps` | `list[_ErasureStepResult]` | One entry per saga step with the rows it touched; a step done by an earlier attempt reads `rows_affected` 0 and a `skipped` note. |
| `requested_at` | `datetime` | When the saga was registered (UTC). |
| `completed_at` | `datetime \| None` | When the saga reached its terminal state (UTC); `None` while it runs. |
| `residue_count` | `int` | Verified forgetting: live rows and bucket objects the post-erasure census still found in scope, per substrate; 0 / {} on a completed saga. |
| `residue` | `dict[str, int]` | Rows still live per table after the saga, only tables with a non-zero count (the Postgres authority's under `pg:<table>`), and the bucket objects left, under the key `objects.document_originals`; `{}` on success. |
| `verified_at` | `datetime \| None` | When the residue census ran (UTC); `None` if it never ran or left a store uncounted (the Postgres authority or the bucket, which the server log names); `residue` then holds what it did count. |
| `census` | `dict[str, int] \| None` | The receipt: every count of this run's census, zeros included; `None` when no census counted every store (none ran, or one left a store uncounted). |
| `purge` | `bool` | Whether the saga deletes rows (true) or tombstones them; a single namespace's never does. |
| `failure_reason` | `str` | Why a failed saga failed, `""` otherwise: `<step>: <error>` or a bare `<error>` outside a step, where `<error>` is the exception's kind or a Loom error's `<CODE>: <message>`, or `verify.residue: ErasureResidueError: residue after erasure… |
| `steps_completed` | `list[str]` | Names of the steps finished so far, sorted. |

## `erasure.status`

Check the status of an in-flight erasure request (queued, running, completed, failed).

`POST /v1/erasure.status` · MCP `loom_erasure_status` · role `viewer` · read · not listed under the MCP `all` toolset

| Input field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `erasure_id` | `str` | required | Id returned by `erasure.request`. |

| Output field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `found` | `bool` | False for an unknown id and for a saga the caller may not read (the two look alike). |
| `erasure_id` | `str` | The saga id asked about. |
| `org` | `str \| None` | The tenant (first element of the identity tuple). |
| `scope_type` | `str \| None` | The saga's scope kind (`user_id`, `namespace` or `namespace_list`); `None` when not found. |
| `scope_value` | `str \| None` | The saga's scope as requested (user id, namespace, or the JSON list). |
| `requester` | `str \| None` | Who asked for the erasure, as given in the request. |
| `status` | `Literal['in_progress', 'completed', 'failed'] \| None` | `in_progress`, `completed` or `failed`; `None` when not found. |
| `current_step` | `int \| None` | How many steps have finished; 99 once the saga completed. |
| `requested_at` | `datetime \| None` | When the saga was registered (UTC). |
| `completed_at` | `datetime \| None` | When the saga reached its terminal state (UTC); `None` while in progress. |
| `failure_reason` | `str \| None` | Why a failed saga failed, `None` otherwise: a reason `erasure.request` names, or `max_attempts (N) exceeded` once recovery gave up, then `; last: <reason>` if any; `the saga failed; the error is in the server log` for a reason in neither… |
| `residue_count` | `int` | Verified forgetting. |
| `residue` | `dict[str, int]` | Rows still live per table at the last census (the Postgres authority's under `pg:<table>`), and the bucket objects left, under the key `objects.document_originals`; `{}` when none. |
| `verified_at` | `datetime \| None` | When the last residue census ran (UTC); `None` if it has not run or left a store uncounted (the Postgres authority or the bucket, which the server log names); `residue` then holds what it did count. |
| `census` | `dict[str, int] \| None` | The receipt: every count of the latest run's census, zeros included; `None` when the latest row holds no census that counted every store (a run in progress, none ran, one left a store uncounted, or a build that keeps no census wrote the… |
| `purge` | `bool` | Whether the saga deletes rows (true) or tombstones them; a single namespace's never does. |
